name: Stare Miasto
tagline: The painted old town, small and entirely walkable
description: A compact hill of pastel tenements, arched gateways and cellar bars, wrapped around the market square and the castle. It is the prettiest part of Lublin and the smallest, so the flats are old, characterful and often awkward. Everything worth walking to is inside ten minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to live inside the postcard and does not mind old plumbing
pros: Every cafe, bar and restaurant within a five-minute walk
Genuinely beautiful streets rather than a reconstructed version
No need for transport at all
cons: Noise from the bars on weekend nights
Old buildings with variable heating and insulation
Almost no parking and limited everyday shopping

name: Srodmiescie
tagline: The centre proper, along the Krakowskie Przedmiescie promenade
description: The commercial and administrative heart, built along a wide pedestrian promenade lined with cafes, milk bars and nineteenth century facades. Offices, the theatre and most of the city's services sit here. Flats are a mix of period buildings and post-war blocks, and the supply is the best in the city.
bestFor: First-time arrivals who want everything reachable on foot and plenty of flats to choose from
pros: The widest choice of apartments at reasonable rents
Cafes with power sockets and reliable fibre in most buildings
cons: Traffic noise on the streets off the promenade
Less charm than the old town a few hundred metres east
Some post-war blocks are tired inside

name: Wieniawa
tagline: Between the centre and the university, quiet and green
description: A residential strip west of the centre running towards the sports stadium and the Saski Garden, with low blocks, mature trees and a calmer pace. It sits within walking distance of both the old town and the main university campuses, which makes it a practical compromise rather than a destination.
bestFor: People who want quiet evenings but a fifteen-minute walk to the centre
pros: Noticeably quieter than the centre at night
Park and stadium on the doorstep
Walking distance to both the centre and the universities
cons: Few restaurants or bars of its own
Housing stock is plain post-war blocks

name: Rury and LSM
tagline: The student quarter, cheapest rents and the UMCS campus
description: A large planned district of 1960s and 70s blocks built around the Maria Curie-Sklodowska university, with wide green spaces between them. This is where most students live and where rents are lowest. It is unglamorous, well served by buses and full of cheap places to eat.
bestFor: Long stays on a tight budget, close to the university social life
pros: The lowest rents in the city
Plenty of cheap canteens, bars and gyms
Large green spaces between the blocks
cons: Twenty minutes by bus to the old town

name: Czechow
tagline: Northern housing estates, family-quiet and well connected
description: A big residential district north of the centre, built as estates around wide roads with supermarkets, schools and a park. Nothing here is picturesque, but the flats are larger than in the centre, the rents are low and the bus links are frequent. It suits a longer, settled stay.
bestFor: Longer stays needing space and a supermarket rather than a bar scene
pros: Everyday shopping and services within walking distance
cons: Nothing to walk to in the evening
Twenty to twenty-five minutes from the old town
